svg.title: Typed rules: the gap CSF and csfc fill
svg.desc: Left: a plain Datalog CS-16 rule matching the strings os/exec and ipc/proc, with three silent failures: a typo matches nothing, a moved directory flags the gateway itself, and two hard-coded copies can drift; the real API list lives as OCaml string literals in go_policy.ml lines 46 to 55. Right: the proc gateway already declared in architecture.csf line 23, a proposed boundary declaration listing the process APIs, and a rule naming the boundary type and gateway; a typo fails to compile, a directory move is one edit, and one declaration replaces both lists. Bottom: a Datalog summary: CSF declares the types, csfc type-checks the rules, Datalog evaluates them.
svg.text: Untyped rules break silently; typed rules fail at compile time
Plain Datalog matches strings. CSF declares the things a rule may name, and csfc checks every rule against those declarations.

text.tspan: % matches nothing: every file passes, forever

svg.text: silent: zero findings looks like success

text.tspan: % the gateway itself is now flagged

svg.text: wrong: the rule outlived the layout

text.tspan: % csfc go_policy.ml:53, and again in house lint

svg.text: Real today: the API list lives as OCaml string literals
CSF + csfc: constants are declared, typed terms
the rule names types, not strings

text.tspan: error: unknown boundary procss (did you mean process?)

svg.text: loud: csfc refuses to compile the rule

text.tspan: every rule naming gateway(proc) follows it

svg.text: safe: rules point at the term, not the path

text.tspan: % read by csfc, house lint, miners
go_policy.ml and the CS-16 copy are generated or gone

svg.text: Also checked: arity, value types, and a rule over an empty relation.

text.tspan: % every constant resolves to a declaration
% declare them in CSF, generate both lists
% so: not "Datalog instead of CSF". CSF is the type system, csfc the checker, Datalog the engine.
